evidence.note: One-sided snowball: after kitchen-sink knee Hall still sits at 132 HP while Hitman is 78 and falling; player never opens a comeback window (final HP [0,115]).
Methodical collar attempts are taxed quickly: collar → 'Hall snaps off grapple counter — Hitman takes 5 damage' (also t12). Pattern feeds CPU momentum rather than creating player offense.
Clear defensive trade-off offered while Hall is on TOP_ROPE: Pull off the top rope 55% is index 1, but methodical selects Hit the ropes and eats missile dropkick for 18 at t20.
Player's only meaningful offense is small: grapple counter 5 damage (t25/t33) and pull-off 6 (t29). No Finish menu ever appears for the player; climax is CPU Razor's Edge KO.
Pacing gate passes (36 in [8,40]) and move_repetition_rate 0.2778 is fine, but the arc is attrition under Hall's control with near_fall_count 0 — no dramatic swing or player climax.
Groggy recovery is clear: after 'Hitman is GROGGY — power moves and finishers are live!' menu offers Shake the cobwebs 66% / Desperation strike 57%; player clears haze successfully.
When grappled, curated menu shows Grapple counter vs Break the grapple with distinct notes — reverse chip vs peel-and-reset.
Pull off the top rope is surfaced as Set up position when Hall is TOP_ROPE — optimal defensive line is not hidden (player simply declines it).
Groggy remains a modifier on STANDING: 'Hitman rises — still groggy from the impact!' with groggy [true, false] before the KO.
single_choice_turns 5 are almost all Fight to your feet-only menus while GROUNDED — readable but binary; no hidden Finish because Hall is never the grounded target on a player turn.
Obvious rematch experiment: take Pull off the top rope at t19 instead of Hit the ropes into the missile.
Curious whether abandoning collar_elbow when behind (and leaning Safe offense / climb) breaks the counter tax that keeps Hall at full health.
Against that, sitting through another methodical get-up grind under a 132→115 Hall lead is only mildly appealing.

stickiness.rematch_reason: Want to test whether taking Pull off top at t19 and skipping early collar re-entries creates any offense/Finish window — but the recorded match itself felt like a controlled squash.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 222 selecting Pull off the top rope at turn 19, then prefer Safe offense or climb over Collar-and-elbow after grapple_counter resets, aiming to ground Hall and open Cover/Sharpshooter.

evidence.note: Groggy beat lands with clear text: 'Hitman is GROGGY — power moves and finishers are live!' after roundhouse kick.
Missile dropkick 18 damage is a solid CPU payoff after the rope run setup.

KO closeout is punchy: 'Hall snaps off razor's edge — Hitman takes 20 damage. Hitman crumples and doesn't move — they are out cold! *** KNOCKOUT — the match is waved off; Hall wins ***' — but no finish_sequence.delays_sec staging (unlike pin/submission).
'Hitman collapses to the canvas — the cover is there for the taking!' teases a pin that never comes; CPU finishes by KO instead (near_fall_count 0).
log_uniqueness_ratio 0.675 is acceptable; player-side logs are mostly get_up / collar / counter chips, so feedback density skews to Hall's offense.

top_issues.summary: One-sided snowball: Hall never drops below 115 HP while Hitman is driven 132→0. Methodical collar→grapple_counter cycles and get_up-only turns produce no player Finish window and no comeback beat.
top_issues.suggested_area: comeback tools when trailing; discourage collar re-entry while clearly behind

top_issues.summary: Turn 34 promises 'the cover is there for the taking!' then turn 36 ends on Razor's Edge knockout with no pin attempt and no finish_sequence delays — cover heat never pays off (near_fall_count 0).
top_issues.suggested_area: CPU pin incentive after collapse/cover tease; KO finish_sequence delays

top_issues.summary: Five single-choice Fight to your feet turns while GROUNDED are correct but deaden decision space for long stretches of the snowball.
top_issues.suggested_area: grounded option variety (desperation/escape) beyond lone get_up
